title: AsyncIterable embeddings client with resumable cursor, typed errors, and graceful shutdown
creator: Priya Rao
description: Goal: Deliver a new embeddings client surface that provides an idiomatic AsyncIterable/AsyncIterator in Python and AsyncIterable in TypeScript with resumable cursor semantics, a clear typed error hierarchy, deterministic retry semantics, per-item cost metadata, and graceful shutdown/backpressure behavior. Background: current embeddings pagination and streaming surfaces mix iterator patterns with ad-hoc resume tokens and opaque error messages that complicate production-grade consumption and observable retries. This ticket implements the client-side contract, wire compatibility with existing pagination tokens, and a migration plan for customers.
acceptance_criteria: Python SDK exposes `Embeddings.async_iter(query, page_size=..., resume_token=None)` returning an async iterator yielding typed items {embedding, id, cost_meta, cursor}
TypeScript SDK exposes `embeddings.stream(query, {pageSize, resumeCursor})` returning an AsyncIterable with the same typed shape
Resume token semantics: tokens are stable across server variants and documented; iterators can be constructed from a token to continue from last yielded item
New error classes documented and surfaced: EmbeddingsTransientError, EmbeddingsThrottlingError, EmbeddingsValidationError, EmbeddingsInternalError
Idempotency and retry behavior deterministic: client retries only for Transient/Throttling errors, with exponential backoff and jitter; resumed iterators do not double-process items when using cursor
Graceful shutdown: iterator.close()/return() signals to cancel inflight requests and persists last-known resume token for resumption
Comprehensive tests: unit, integration against test server, and e2e load-test to verify memory stability and latency under backpressure
Docs and migration guide published in SDK changelog and Console docs
comments: 2026-02-12: Initial spike showed that resumable cursor needs an explicit per-item sequence number to avoid duplicates when batch sizes change. Decided to include sequence_id in token payload.
2026-02-18: Design review with DX. Agreed on typed response shape `{id, embedding: number[], cost_meta: {tokens: int, model: string}, cursor}` for parity across languages.

2026-02-23: Engineering review noted potential large memory growth if consumer iterates slower than production throughput. Plan: expose backpressure via optional `high_water_mark` and pause on underlying connection when exceeded.

2026-03-01: PoC for Python async iterator implemented. Needs deterministic close semantics for async generators (calling `aclose()` on Python 3.11). Adding explicit `close()` wrapper and `resume_token()` accessor.

2026-03-06: PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/4923 - implements TS AsyncIterable and Python async iterator with basic resume token encoding. Feature flags added behind `embAsyncIterableV2`.
2026-03-10: Code review feedback from Lina (DX): split typed error classes into separate exports, add `isRetryable(err)` helper, and include `status_code` and `retry_after` in Throttling error.

2026-03-12: Load tests (100 concurrent iterators, 2k queries/sec) passed with P95 latency improvement of 18% using batching + backpressure; memory leak trace resolved by explicitly closing generator on consumer exceptions.
Follow-ups: add telemetry tags so Console can group errors by `error_class` and `resume_token_present` for regression alerting. Add migration script examples for Node and Python.
test_plan: Unit tests for token encode/decode, sequence_id ordering, and typed error mapping
Integration tests against local test server verifying resume behavior with shifted batch sizes
Stress tests: 500 concurrent clients iterating at variable speeds to validate backpressure and memory stability
Chaos test: inject transient 503 and ensure retries only trigger where appropriate and no duplicate items are delivered when resuming
Cross-language acceptance: Node and Python sample apps consuming the iterator and resuming from tokens
migration_notes: Backwards compatibility: server will accept v1 tokens and translate to v2 by mapping sequence offsets. Consumers using naive pagination via numeric offsets should migrate to cursor API. Provide sample scripts: `python -m redwood.embeddings.resume_from_token <token>` and `node scripts/resume-embeddings.js <cursor>`.
compatibility_plan: Release TS and Python SDKs simultaneously behind feature flag `embAsyncIterableV2`. Default remains v1 for two weeks while we monitor Console telemetry; then flip flag for beta customers and gather feedback before full rollout. Maintain server-side translation for 90 days.
rollout_plan: alpha: internal SDK + docs, feature flag off (this week)
beta: enable for selected customers and SDK opt-in (week +2)
gradual: expand to 25% production traffic with automatic fallback to v1 tokens (week +4)
full: flip default and publish migration guide (week +6)

Add Console panels for resume success rate and iterator memory usage
